submitted.rationale: Index 23 (Mg0.33Sb0.67, MgSb2O6 stoichiometry) gave the highest measured EQE (0.0173%). MgSb2O6 is on the MACE hull, and its predicted HSE gap (2.8 eV) is below the 3.2 eV illumination.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0014%, an order of magnitude lower
Mg-rich phases such as Mg4Sb2O9 are predicted to have wide gaps (4.2 eV), so they would not absorb 3.2 eV light. Measured EQE also fell from Sb 0.67 to Sb 0.56.

consultations.verdict: Support: MgSb2O6 (trirutile, on hull per MACE) has predicted HSE gap 2.82 eV < 3.2 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; Mg-rich phases (Mg4Sb2O9 4.2 eV) do not. Index 23 sits at MgSb2O6 stoichiometry.
Support: Sb-richer MgSb4O10-type phase predicted HSE gap 1.2 eV, stronger visible/UV absorption than MgSb2O6; index 26 (Sb 0.76) is the most Sb-rich available and moves toward that region.

Weak support: Mg2Sb3O8 (Sb 0.6) predicted to have a near-zero gap, so it absorbs strongly but may be defect-/metal-like. Mg3SbO4 (3.07 eV) is only marginally absorbing. Index 19 (Sb 0.555) is the GP-UCB pick and explores the mid-composition region where the model predicts absorbing phases.
